subject: Configurable tenant TTL & geo-tagged storage: FinBridge compliance ask
messages:
From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@finbridge.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Configurable tenant retention and region-pinning — initial ask

Hi Michael,

Thanks for taking the time on the call earlier. To recap FinBridge's compliance needs and to help your product/eng teams size the work, here are the main asks from Legal/InfoSec: 

- Per-tenant configurable TTL for user-generated data, embeddings, and model context (ability to set 30/90/365/indefinite).
- Option to pin storage of a tenant's data and derived artifacts to an EU region (data-at-rest must remain in EU).
- Proof of deletion and an auditable deletion event (delete receipt) when TTL expires or when we trigger a manual purge.
- Ability to place a legal hold on a tenant (suspend deletion) and export associated audit logs.

We are starting a pilot with one EU-regulated product team and need a clear mutual action plan, timeline, and any compliance artifacts you can provide (SOC2 evidence we can include, sample deletion receipts).

Attached: FinBridge_data_controls_checklist.pdf (high level checklist from Legal).

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-tenant TTL today, and if not, what the earliest realistic timeline is for a production-grade implementation? Also, can you share any performance/cost implications for pinning data to a specific region?

Thanks,
Emma Johnson
Head of InfoSec Programs
FinBridge
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@finbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Configurable tenant retention and region-pinning — initial ask

Emma — thanks for the clear checklist, this is exactly the kind of detail we need. Short answers up front: we do not currently offer first-class per-tenant TTL gating in the hosted product (we have org-level retention knobs and account-level routing), and we can implement EU-region pinning for storage + KV/embeddings with a defined rollout.

Couple of clarification questions for scope/roadmap sizing: 
- Granularity: do you need separate TTLs for raw input, embeddings, and model-generated outputs, or is a single tenant-level TTL sufficient?
- Legal hold behavior: should a legal hold stop automated purges but keep ingestion/serving active, or should it also suspend writes?
- Export format: what format does your audit team want for deletion receipts (simple JSON event, signed text file, or PDF letter)?
- Scale: expected number of tenants and tokens stored for pilot (ballpark weekly ingestion).

From an engineering perspective, the core pieces we'd need to implement: TTL metadata on tenant objects, a region-aware storage selector for cold storage and embedding blobs, scheduled purge workers with audit-event emission, and a legal-hold flag that gates purge workflows. I'll loop in Monica and Karthik to propose a minimal roadmap and rough timeline.

Attachments: retention_matrix_proposal.xlsx (internal quick matrix — WIP).

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@finbridge.com>
Date: 2027-05-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Configurable tenant retention and region-pinning — initial ask

Looping in product/eng detail from our side. Hi Emma — appreciate the checklist, and welcome. Internal notes below for clarity and to set expectations.

Design assumptions we propose:
- Tenant-level TTL with optional per-artifact overrides (embedding, logs, model outputs). Default to tenant TTL unless override present.
- Geo-tagging: a tenant record can be pinned to a region label (eu-west-1, eu-central-1). All new blobs/embeddings will be routed accordingly; existing data at time of flip will be migrated lazily or archived depending on size.
- Audit & receipts: each purge operation will emit a signed JSON event and a human-readable text receipt; retention of audit logs will be configurable (we recommend 7 years for audit logs if needed).
- Legal hold: flag on tenant that pauses purge workers; API to apply/remove hold with audit trail.

Rough roadmap (proposal):
- Week 1–3: design spec + API wireframes (admin UI + tenant API)
- Week 4–8: core storage routing + TTL metadata + purge worker prototype (internal staging)
- Week 9–12: audit events, deletion receipt generator, legal hold gating, EU pilot in eu-west-1
- Week 13–16: canary roll, docs, compliance artifacts (SOC2 checklist mapping), handoff to success/ops

Impacts/costs: embedding pinning will require additional cross-region replication considerations for model caches — expect a modest increase in storage and a potential latency trade for cross-region reads if not colocated. We can mitigate with caching strategies.

Questions for Emma:
1) Acceptance criteria for the pilot (what constitutes "complete" from FinBridge legal/engineering perspective)
2) Any constraints on migration windows (do you need zero-downtime migration of historical data?)

Attaching: tenant_retention_API_wireframe.png (admin UI sketch).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Product — Core Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@finbridge.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T07:51:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Configurable tenant retention and region-pinning — initial ask

Monica / Michael — thanks, that roadmap looks reasonable. To answer your questions: 

- Granularity: we need distinct TTLs for embeddings vs raw inputs. Embeddings are considered derived data and our policy treats them differently.
- Legal hold behavior: legal hold should pause all automated deletions but allow reads; writes can continue (we may still need to retain ingestion metadata).
- Deletion receipt: signed JSON event is fine; procurement will want a human-readable confirmation for audit purposes. A simple text receipt is acceptable as long as it includes tenant id, timestamp, scope, and a signature.
- Pilot acceptance: successful pilot = (1) tenant pinned to EU region with storage verified, (2) automated purge fired correctly for test TTL with audit event present, (3) manual legal hold applied/removed with audit trail, (4) deletion receipt generated and verified by our audit team.
- Migration: we cannot afford extended downtime; prefer lazy migration with archive fallback.

Procurement looping in: procurement@finbridge.com — they will coordinate a pilot SOW if we move forward.

Subject: Re: Configurable tenant retention and region-pinning — initial ask

Internal summary & action items (for roadmap / eng kickoff):

Summary of FinBridge asks (acceptance criteria):
- Per-tenant TTL with separate controls for embeddings and raw inputs.
- EU-region pinning for storage at tenant level; lazy migration preferred.
- Signed JSON deletion receipts + human-readable text confirmation.
- Legal hold flag that pauses purge workers but allows reads/writes to continue.

Action items and owners:
- Monica: finalize API + admin UI wireframes; include tenant-level TTL + per-artifact override controls. Target spec complete by 2027-05-23. (related: JIRA-INF-592)
- Karthik: prototype storage routing and purge worker logic (stage). Wire up audit-event emission. Target prototype by 2027-06-06.
- Michael: prepare compliance mapping doc (SOC2 mapping + sample deletion receipt) and coordinate pilot acceptance criteria with FinBridge procurement. Target deliverable by 2027-05-25. Attach sample audit-delete-sample.txt for FinBridge to review.
- Ops/Infra (follow-up): confirm eu-west-1 capacity and quantify cross-region replication cost delta for embedding pinning.

Notes: prioritize signed JSON receipts with a simple text fallback. For pilot, we'll scope migration as "lazy": leave existing data until requested; provide export tooling in case FinBridge wants immediate migration.

Attachments: audit-delete-sample.txt (example deletion event), retention_matrix_proposal.xlsx (updated).

I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to review the spec; Monica please propose slots.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
